alt.en: A detail of an old printed magazine column. It begins "Another pulling song of almost equal popularity in old days was the following one:", then two short lines of music, marked "Solo. Moderato." and "Chorus.", with the words "Way, haul away, haul away, my Josie." and "Way, haul away, haul away, Joe." under the notes. At the foot: "These have, as is seen, but a single chorus. Their purely nautical origin is manifest, and they are undoubtedly very old."
alt.es: Detalle de una columna impresa de una revista antigua. Empieza "Another pulling song of almost equal popularity in old days was the following one:", y siguen dos líneas cortas de música, marcadas "Solo. Moderato." y "Chorus.", con las palabras "Way, haul away, haul away, my Josie." y "Way, haul away, haul away, Joe." bajo las notas. Al pie: "These have, as is seen, but a single chorus. Their purely nautical origin is manifest, and they are undoubtedly very old."

caption.en: William L. Alden's "Sailor Songs" in Harper's New Monthly Magazine, July 1882, page 282: "another pulling song of almost equal popularity in old days", with the solo "my Josie" and the chorus landing on "Joe", the earliest printing of this shanty we found.
caption.es: "Sailor Songs", de William L. Alden, en Harper's New Monthly Magazine, julio de 1882, página 282: "otra canción para halar casi igual de popular en los viejos tiempos", con el verso del solista "my Josie" y el estribillo que cae en "Joe", la impresión más antigua de esta shanty que hemos encontrado.

source: William L. Alden, "Sailor Songs", Harper's New Monthly Magazine, vol. 65, no. 386 (New York: Harper & Brothers, July 1882), p. 282, detail of the right column (from "Another pulling song of almost equal popularity" to "undoubtedly very old."; the Bowline above it is left out)

licenceEvidence: Printed in Harper's New Monthly Magazine, New York, July 1882 (running head "282 HARPER'S NEW MONTHLY MAGAZINE."); author William Livingston Alden died 1908. alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a three-masted sailing ship riding in calm water, seen from the bow. Its sails are off, and the bare yards cross each mast in tiers, with a web of rigging running down to the deck. A cable runs from the bow down into the water, and a low, flat shore lies on the horizon.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de un velero de tres palos en aguas tranquilas, visto desde la proa. No lleva las velas puestas, y las vergas desnudas cruzan cada palo en hileras, con una red de jarcia que baja hasta la cubierta. Un cable sale de la proa y se hunde en el agua, y en el horizonte hay una costa baja y llana.

caption.en: The Glasgow-built full-rigged ship Samoena, photographed by Allan C. Green about 1900 to 1912: on ships like her, the tacks and sheets this shanty pulled held down the corners of the big square sails.
caption.es: El velero de tres palos Samoena, construido en Glasgow y de aparejo redondo, fotografiado por Allan C. Green hacia 1900-1912: en barcos como este, las amuras y las escotas de las que se halaba con esta shanty sujetaban los puños de las grandes velas cuadras.

source: Samoena [picture] / Allan C. Green (glass negative, half plate, 12.1 x 16.6 cm; Allan C. Green collection of glass negatives)

alt.en: The top of a printed music page headed "XXVII. Haul Away, Joe.", with a voice line over a two-staff piano part in three rows. The words run "Haul away, haul away, haul away, my Rosie, Way, haul away, haul away, Joe.", then, marked Solo, "O you talk about your Aver* girls, And round the corner Sally;", then, marked Chorus, "Way, haul away, haul away, Joe." A small arrowhead stands over each "Joe", and a footnote reads "* i.e. Havre."
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página de música impresa con el encabezado "XXVII. Haul Away, Joe.", con la línea de la voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, en tres filas. La letra dice "Haul away, haul away, haul away, my Rosie, Way, haul away, haul away, Joe.", luego, marcado Solo, "O you talk about your Aver* girls, And round the corner Sally;", y luego, marcado Chorus, "Way, haul away, haul away, Joe." Sobre cada "Joe" hay una pequeña punta de flecha, y una nota al pie dice "* i.e. Havre."

caption.en: No. XXVII of Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (1914), page 32: the dorian tune John Short of Watchet sang, with Sharp's piano part and an arrowhead over each "Joe" where the crew pulled, the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: El n.º XXVII de English Folk-Chanteys, de Cecil Sharp (1914), página 32: la melodía dórica que cantaba John Short, de Watchet, con el acompañamiento de piano de Sharp y una punta de flecha sobre cada "Joe", donde tiraba la tripulación; es la página de la que sale nuestro arreglo.

source: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys (London: Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co. and Schott & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott & Pearce, 1914), No. XXVII, "Haul Away, Joe", p. 32, upper part (the music only; the verses below are not shown)
